features: Complete narrow flattened oblong frond around a continuous central axis, gentle taper to tip and blunt basal attachment
About three dozen angled lateral ridges/structures joined through common basal frond rather than independent comb branches or fern leaflets
Subtle irregular pustules on one side only; no unpreserved tentacles or settled cnidarian/modern sea-pen classification
thaumaptilon.claim: Evidence-informed whole-organism outline reconstruction of Thaumaptilon walcotti, not a modern sea pen or exact specimen replica. Nominal212mm height references ROM complete holotype USNM468028; width50mm follows reported maximum, thickness/color/pose are artistic. Morphological affinity remains disputed: ROM describes historical stem-cnidarian interpretation, Hoyal Cuthill2022 supports Petalonamae. Neither is asserted as settled. Basal anchoring interpretation and pustules-as-zooids uncertain; no feeding tentacles invented.
thaumaptilon.decisions: Actual concept has correct connected narrow lamina and short blunt base, but is overly symmetrical and overregular. Retain continuous full-volume frond, subtly unequal lateral structures and low relief on both broad surfaces, sparse haphazard pustules on front only. Eighteen oblique structures each side as approximate about-three-dozen layout, not fossil-count assertion. No open negative spaces between structures: connected common sheet. Short basal attachment remains partly frond-like and blunt, not a big modern sea-pen bulb or plant roots. Rear has angled relief but no pustules. Thin solid cross-section, gentle bent pose, no rock slab or environment base.
thaumaptilon.observation: Complete ROM part/counterpart photographs personally inspected: broad continuous dark frond, strong axial zone, gently curved oblong outline, shallow angled lateral structures rather than independent protruding leaves; basal region irregular and blunt. Primary Hoyal Cuthill2022 Fig2 personally inspected: offset oblique lines around demarked axial band and texture continuing into inferred basal region, supporting cautious basal treatment. Color and living cross-section unpreserved. Thumbnail alone was inadequate and not treated as complete evidence.

features: One thin tall elongated unperforated joint-bounded rock wall, broad vertical faces and narrow thickness
Irregular erosion-notched crest, asymmetric ends and modest wider foot; no caprock pedestal or rounded hoodoo
Broad sandstone strata support structure; no arch hole or exact named-site/age assertion
sandstone-fin.claim: Generic sandstone fin teaching prop, not a replica of Wooden Shoe Arch or an Arches locality. NPS describes joint fracturing and weathering producing fins before arch perforation. Nominal16x2x10m dimensions, crest and bedding are artistic; no exact formation age or composition claimed.
sandstone-fin.decisions: Concept fin wall proportions, planar faces, narrow top and unperforated silhouette retained; exclude generated phototexture and excessive tiny cracks. Continuous closed wall prism with variable thickness, irregular vertical joint grooves confined to surface and uneven long crest. Warm broad band colors, restrained broad relief, no repeated bricks, no disconnected blocks, no broad base pedestal.
sandstone-fin.observation: Actual NPS Wooden Shoe interpretive sequence pixels inspected: parallel cracks divide layered sandstone into thin long walls before holes and spires emerge; stage2-3 wall/fin morphology supports unperforated fin. Sequence-specific dates and site not transferred to generic asset.

features: Bulbous steep-sided compact extrusion with broad irregular summit, no summit crater
Angular interlocking blocky rind with irregular fractures and a subordinate basal rubble apron
Asymmetric closed solid dome, not smooth cinder cone, uniformly spherical boulder pile or glowing eruption
lava-dome.claim: Generic lava dome morphology teaching prop supported by NPS viscous extrusion and blocky brecciated surface descriptions. Actual Novarupta photographs consulted only for general form; not a named volcano, event or measured replica. Nominal120x100x45m scale and colors artistic. Static cooled surface, no current hazard or live eruption assertion.
lava-dome.decisions: Concept dome mass, high shoulders and angular rind retained. Exclude excessive photo-like pebble microdetail and arbitrary blocks at every face. Author one closed uneven radial mass with purposeful large blocky lobes and limited embedded angular surface outcrops, quieter upper planes and stronger side fractures; varied smaller rubble at contact skirt. No concave crater, snow, smoke, glow, exact photographed outline or surrounding terrain.
lava-dome.observation: Actual NPS/USGS Novarupta overall photo inspected: steep rounded squat mass with near-vertical upper shoulders, irregular broad summit and talus at foot, not conical crater. Actual USGS Cyrus Read rubble photo inspected: angular fractured coherent rock surfaces and mixed-size rubbly fragments, no smooth lava skin.

features: Connected irregular polygon terrain network with variable cell sizes and orientations, not perfect hex tiles or mudcracks
Coherent low-centered morphology: wetter lower centers inside raised hummocky rims with narrow connected crest grooves
One solid closed soil terrain module with shallow meaningful surface relief; generic nominal scale, no named site or current climate trend
ice-wedge-polygon-ground.claim: Generic low-centered ice-wedge polygon ground teaching module. NPS Swanson explains contraction cracks, repeated freezing and raised margins around lower wetter centers; aerial photos establish irregular connected networks. Nominal45x40m footprint,3m cut soil section and0.7m relief artistic, not surveyed study site, age or current permafrost trend. Ice wedges are buried, no exposed surface ice required.
ice-wedge-polygon-ground.decisions: Concept low centers/raised rims and connected irregular cells retained. Override approximately regular equal-size cells with clipped irregular Voronoi cells of unequal size, four-to-seven sides and broken orientations. One continuous manifold heightfield using shared cell boundary vertices, paired near-boundary elevated shoulders and thin lower contraction groove; centers remain below shoulders but above soil base. No floating tiled plates, deep mudcrack gaps, mixed high-centered cells, blue lakes, snow or plants. Side cut surfaces close full terrain volume.
ice-wedge-polygon-ground.observation: Actual NPS Yukon aerial polygon image and NPS Matt Nolan Bering Land Bridge aerial photo personally inspected: dense irregular connected dark boundaries surround unequal polygon areas; not regular decorative hexagons. NPS Swanson primary morphology text distinguishes low-centered raised margins from high-centered degraded margins; low-centered subtype chosen explicitly, no contemporary trend inference.
